survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD report is primarily a methodological synthesis and proof-of-concept demonstrations of measurement invariance procedures across groups (countries, time points) using multigroup CFA/IRT and latent class models. For the empirical illustrations, the report describes that survey weights were not taken into account in the ESS-based marginal Bayesian measurement invariance example, and it discusses two possible ways to incorporate weights (pseudo-likelihood weighting of the likelihood vs. weighting latent responses) as future work. In the ESS longitudinal illustration, missing values are specified (e.g., coded as 77/88/99) and handled within the modelling framework, but the report does not provide a full complex-survey weighting specification for all chapters. For practitioners applying these methods to PISA/TALIS/PIAAC microdata, the recommended approach is to use the appropriate sampling weights from the international database when available, and to treat weight integration as an additional modelling step because several Bayesian random-parameter invariance models are not straightforward to combine with complex survey design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report focuses on measurement invariance testing for questionnaire scales and latent constructs using multigroup CFA/IRT and latent class models, rather than estimating PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. While some chapters specify missing-value codes for the ESS illustration, the report does not provide a complete, generalizable missing-data handling strategy (e.g., listwise vs. multiple imputation) across all demonstrations and simulated studies. Therefore, missing-data handling is treated as not reported at the report level.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report uses multiple demonstrations rather than a single unified analytic sample. For the ESS-based MGCFA/alignment illustration, it uses longitudinal (repeated cross-sectional) ESS data from France across seven rounds (2002–2014) and specifies missing-value codes (77/88/99) for the selected items measuring willingness to allow immigrants (latent variable ALLOW). For the ESS-based Bayesian approximate measurement invariance illustration, it uses ESS round 2002 data across 22 countries and focuses on three ALLOW items (imsmetn, imdfetn, impcntr). For the ESS-based Bayesian marginal measurement invariance testing, it draws balanced samples from selected ESS countries (fixed groups: Belgium and Sweden; random groups: Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, Switzerland), samples a fixed number of response observations per country, dichotomises the 0–10 response scales, and explicitly notes that additional sampling weights were not taken into account. For the TALIS-based latent class analysis illustration, it uses TALIS 2013 principal ratings from 38 countries (n=7,436 principals) and applies multigroup and multilevel LCA to five school participation items (TC2G22A–TC2G22E), treating countries as groups and principals nested within countries.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report addresses measurement invariance in large-scale cross-cultural surveys (PISA, TALIS, PIAAC) and explains why conventional exact invariance tests (e.g., MGCFA scalar invariance, IRT DIF tests) can be overly strict or unstable when many groups are compared. It presents and applies proof-of-concept procedures using both real and simulated data: multigroup CFA with alignment optimisation, Bayesian approximate measurement invariance (BSEM/approximate MI with alignment), Bayesian marginal measurement invariance testing in a one-parameter IRT framework (using fractional Bayes factors), and multigroup/multilevel latent class analysis for categorical latent variables. Across demonstrations, the report shows that scalar invariance often fails under strict criteria, while alignment and Bayesian approximate/marginal approaches can still support meaningful cross-group comparisons by quantifying evidence for (approximate) invariance and by avoiding anchor-item dependence. For example, in the ESS-based ALLOW illustration, scalar invariance fit is poor under traditional MGCFA, whereas Bayesian approximate MI with alignment yields highly correlated factor-mean rankings (correlations >0.98) with sensitivity to prior variance for some country pairs. The report emphasizes that these methods are promising but not yet definitive standards, and it highlights limitations such as sensitivity to priors, computational complexity, and challenges incorporating complex survey weights.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a methodological report rather than an empirical predictive ML study: it does not train or evaluate machine-learning models to predict student outcomes, and it does not define PV-based achievement targets. Consequently, ML technique fields are intentionally empty and main_findings are not populated. The report includes several empirical illustrations (ESS and TALIS) and simulation studies, but the focus is on statistical invariance testing and model fit/evidence for measurement comparability rather than predictive performance metrics.
